chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Maysarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Two things with which people corrupt their prayers: The man's saying, 'Blessed is Your name and Exalted is Your majesty,' and it is merely something the jinn said out of ignorance, which God quoted from them; and the man's saying, 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God.'

key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ الل: A phrase meaning 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God,' often recited incorrectly in the middle of prayer.
key_terms.الْجِنُّ: The jinn, whose ignorant utterance is quoted by God.
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ: A phrase meaning 'Blessed is Your name and Exalted is Your majesty,' cited as a jinnic utterance quoted in the Quran.
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُمْ: Their prayers, which are described as being corrupted by these actions.

ai.seo_question: What two phrases corrupt the validity of prayer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifying two common innovations that corrupt the validity of prayer: the phrase 'Tabaraka ismuka wa ta'ala jadduka,' which the Imam attributes to the jinn's ignorant speech quoted in the Quran, and the premature recitation of 'As-salamu alayna wa ala ibadillah as-salihin' before the final Tashahhud. This highlights the Shia emphasis on adhering strictly to the Prophetic and Imami liturgical structure, distinguishing between divine revelation and cultural accretions in worship.
